root_cause.poll-savepoll-not-purge-marked: savePoll for an OPEN poll was a get-then-set through enqueue and allocateVoteSeq a get-then-set of few:poll-vote-seq:<g>; neither ran in a transaction nor checked the in-memory purgedGroups mark that clearPollData sets, so a poll open / vote cast in flight for a left group re-created few:polls:<g> / few:poll-vote-seq:<g> after the purge.
root_cause.receipt-clock: Not applicable: few:poll-receipt-clock is ONE global key (RECEIPT_CLOCK_KEY), not scoped to any group. clearPollData never deletes it (only clearAllPollData does), so no left-group data can be re-created through it and it carries no group identifier. No change.

fix.savePoll_open: Read-upsert-write in ONE pollTxn readwrite transaction inside enqueue(key); first statement checks purgedGroups.has(poll.groupId) and writes nothing. Resolves null when nothing was written; postStoreChanged only after a write. Closed path untouched. Side effect: a non-array stored value is now treated as an empty list instead of throwing.
fix.allocateVoteSeq: Read-max-increment-write in ONE pollTxn inside enqueue(key) under the unchanged Web Locks wrapper; throws inside the transaction on a purged group, so the transaction aborts, nothing is written and the call REJECTS (pollCast then sends nothing - fail closed; its existing failed-allocation path).
fix.handleOpen: Returns early when deps.savePoll resolves exactly null (nothing stored, nothing to replay, no version bump). Mocks resolving undefined keep the old flow.
fix.createPoll_and_pollCast: Unchanged: pollCast already propagates an allocation rejection; PollStoreContext.createPoll's optimistic setPolls for a group being left is cosmetic and was left alone (minimal change).
fix.release: releasePollPurgeMark (join choke point) and clearAllPollData remain the only releases.

2 allocation fault-injection cases (read fails / write fails) moved from mocked idb get/set to the transaction faults (txnFaults.failGet on few:poll-vote-seq:, failCommit), because allocateVoteSeq now runs in one pollTxn; an unconsumed get mockImplementationOnce had cascaded into a third test.

verification_answers.VQ-1: YES. pollPurgeMarkWrites.test.ts (real idb-keyval over fake-indexeddb) failed 6 of 10 before the fix (savePoll after purge, savePoll queued before the purge, update of a stored open poll, allocateVoteSeq after purge / queued before purge / re-join cycle) and passes after; row absence asserted on few:polls:<g> and few:poll-vote-seq:<g>. NB the report's key name few:poll-seq-reservations:<g> is wrong; the real key is few:poll-vote-seq:<g> (SEQ_RESERVATIONS_PREFIX).
verification_answers.VQ-2: YES. The purgedGroups check is the first statement of the pollTxn body (same transaction as the put) for both writers, in enqueue like the queues/saveVoteIfNewer. Only releasePollPurgeMark and clearAllPollData delete from the set (unchanged); tests show savePoll and allocateVoteSeq work again after releasePollPurgeMark and that the purge dropped the old reservation (seq restarts at 1).
verification_answers.VQ-3: YES. allocateVoteSeq rejects with /purged/ so castPollVote/pollCast sends nothing (existing fail-closed path); handleOpen returns early on null with no replay/version bump/error (new unit test); createPoll just gets null back from savePoll (no crash; optimistic UI state for a group being left left as is). Receipt clock shown to be global and not group-scoped (root_cause.receipt-clock).

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The report named the reservation key few:poll-seq-reservations:<g> but the real key is few:poll-vote-seq:<g>; my first repro asserted absence of a non-existent key (vacuously true post-fix) and only the reject assertion caught it, so a wrong key in a bug report can silently weaken a 'row must not exist' test.
